## 2020
September: The Trump administration says it is cutting aid to Ethiopia over its move to begin filling the dam before reaching an agreement with Egypt and Sudan. Ethiopia seeks clarification from the US on its aid cut, but says it will not affect bilateral relations. An Ethiopian diplomat says his country wants to resume GERD talks, Addis Ababa starts sending positive messages to Sudan and Egypt. Ethiopia's prime minister says his country has no intention of harming Sudan and Egypt with the dam's construction. The three countries, however, fail to resume talks scheduled for mid-September. At a meeting two weeks later, they disagree on a draft paper prepared by their negotiating teams as requested by the AU, with Sudan suggesting a greater role in the drafting of the paper by the AU and observers, including the EU and US. Earlier in September, Sudan and Egypt issue flood warnings amid concerns over rising water levels in the Nile. Sudan declares a national state of emergency for three months after more than 100 people died and thousands were displaced due to the heavy floods in early September. Sudanese irrigation ministry says flooding caused by heavy seasonal rain, mostly in Ethiopia, that led the Nile River to rise about 17.5 metres, its highest level in about a century.

## 2020
October: AU-led dam talks resume towards the end of October after a seven-week break with a virtual meeting between the foreign and irrigation ministers of the three countries upon an invitation from South Africa, the current AU chair, to discuss how to restart negotiations. AU praises talks over the dam. This came few days after international organisations stepped in to revive stalled negotiations, with the Inter-Governmental Authority on Development (IGAD), EU and UN voicing support for AU-led talks. Egyptian and Sudanese leaders stress from Cairo the two countries' adherence to a "binding" deal. Egyptian officials earlier called for resuming the talks, stressing the need to reach a binding agreement. Egypt's water minister says lack of deal on Ethiopian dam poses "a challenge" to his country and its limited water resources. The minister, however, says that his country has "mechanisms and scenarios to diplomatically deal with the GERD issue in case of negotiations failure". Ethiopia reacts angrily to Trump's remarks during a phone call with the leaders of Sudan and Israel, blaming Ethiopia for the failure of dam talks and saying that Egypt will "end up blowing up the dam". Ethiopian prime minister's office says nothing "can stop us" and "Ethiopia will not cave in to aggression of any kind". Ethiopia summons the US ambassador to "clarify" Trump's remarks. Ethiopians launch worldwide online petition to protest against Trump's comments. Ethiopia once again stressed that the second phase of filling the dam will "proceed as planned". Ethiopia's president reveals that two turbines will start early generation, and water minister says Nile dam has reached 76.35% completion. Ethiopia bans all flights over the dam to avoid security threats, following remarks by the country's air force commander that it is capable of foiling any attempted attack the dam. Days later, Ethiopia's prime minister says deadly attacks in a region bordering Sudan sought to derail the dam's construction, and the army says it has "destroyed" gangs of "bandits" stationed near the GERD.

## 2020
November: Protracted negotiations between the three countries resume through a virtual meeting between their irrigation ministers, experts and international mediators, but no agreement is reached on a methodology for talks to continue. Reports suggest that the talks move forward as legal and technical committee members from the three countries conclude meetings on creating a framework for negotiations. The three countries agree to continue talks through a six-member team that includes two members from each country, to develop a reference framework for the role of experts in facilitating negotiations. Ethiopia, however, says the three countries are unable to reach a complete agreement on the agenda for the talks, but have agreed to consult with the AU moving forward. Ethiopia also says Egypt refuses to accept a call by Ethiopia and Sudan for a greater AU role in the talks. Two weeks later, the foreign and irrigation ministers of the three countries hold a virtual meeting. They agree on the need to continue talks mediated by the AU. As a border dispute breaks out between Ethiopia and Sudan, the latter moves closer to Egypt. Egyptian-Sudanese armed forces conduct joint drills dubbed the Nile Eagles 1 in Sudan in late November. Sudanese army re-deploys its forces in the agricultural area of al-Fashaga in the eastern al-Qadarif state, where Ethiopian farmers have been cultivating land claimed by Sudan.
December: Sudan and Ethiopia engage in active diplomacy and exchange official visits as they discuss ways to resume dam talks. Sudanese and Ethiopian prime ministers hold talks in Addis Ababa on the dam dispute and the Tigray conflict. Sudanese and Ethiopian water ministers discuss in Khartoum ways to resume dam talks in the near future with a greater role for experts from the AU. President Sisi says in an interview to French newspaper Le Figaro that "filling the dam in violation of international law and rules threatens water supply to 100 million Egyptians". Egypt summons Ethiopian charge d'affaires in Cairo to explain statements made by his foreign ministry's spokesman described as interfering in "Egyptian internal affairs". Ethiopia denies Egypt has summoned its diplomat.
* * *

## 2021
January: Sudan boycotts talks with Ethiopia for the second time since November over fears that current methods will not produce an agreement. A virtual meeting between Egypt, Sudan and Ethiopia fails to materialise due to Sudan's absence. But a week later, the foreign and water ministers of Ethiopia, Egypt and Sudan hold a virtual meeting, which ends without an agreement. Ethiopia blames Sudan for failure of talks. Ethiopia rejects any deal restricting its right to use Nile water, and accuses Sudan and Egypt of "deliberately delaying" dam talks. Sudan's cabinet expresses concern over possible refilling of the dam. Ethiopia says new AU chair to preside over dam negotiations. The three countries, especially Sudan and Egypt, engage in active foreign diplomacy to explain their stances on the dam. A UAE delegation visits Sudan to break deadlock. Sudanese delegation visits South Africa and Kenya to discuss border and dam disputes with Ethiopia. The first vice-chairman of Sudan's Sovereign Council discusses Ethiopia border and dam disputes with Qatar's foreign minister. Sudan's water minister briefs French and Russian ambassadors about the latest GERD developments. Egyptian president discusses dam with US, AU and Sudanese officials. In a meeting with AU Commission chairman, President Sisi renews his rejection of any impact on Egypt's Nile water rights. Ethiopian and Austrian foreign ministers discuss border dispute with Sudan and the dam. Ethiopia's water minister says dam's construction "progressing as planned" amid impasse over its filling.
February: Egypt and the Arab Parliament back Sudan's proposal to form an AU-led international quadripartite mediation team that includes the US, the EU and the UN to mediate in the dam dispute and revive stalled dam talks. Khartoum recalls its ambassador from Addis Ababa. Egypt and Sudan reportedly consider "withdrawing" from dam declaration. Ethiopia accuses Sudan of engaging in "provocative behaviour", which it claims is "being fuelled by a third party" - an implicit reference to Egypt. Egypt and Sudan warn Ethiopia over the unilateral filling of the dam before a tripartite agreement is reached. Ethiopia and South Sudan sign a military cooperation deal, in an apparent response to military cooperation between Egypt and Sudan. Several mediators, including the EU, also step in to defuse tension and help resume talks. Egypt gets support from some Arab countries, as the Arab League chief and the AU Commission chairman reject "unilateral measures" over Ethiopian dam.

## 2021
March: Cairo and Khartoum continue to develop increasingly closer security cooperation and diplomatic coordination of stances on the GERD. They urge Ethiopia to return to dam talks and express concern over the stalemate in the talks. Sudanese top diplomat Mariam al-Sadiq al-Mahdi holds talks in Cairo with her Egyptian counterpart and President Sisi, who stresses the "inevitability" of reaching a legally binding agreement. Mahdi says Egypt and Sudan have agreed to coordinate stances and launch a campaign to explain to African leaders the danger of Ethiopia's unilateral filling of the dam. Both countries' top diplomats stress that Ethiopia's "execution of the second phase of the unilateral filling of the GERD will represent an immediate threat to Egypt and Sudan's water security". Days later, President Sisi visits Sudan and meets the chairman of the Sovereign Council, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan. They agree to reject any unilateral move by Addis Ababa to fill and activate the dam to "impose the status quo and monopolise the resources of the Blue Nile". The Sudanese prime minister also visits Cairo and stresses the need to reach an understanding over the dam. Sisi reiterates Egypt's support for the Sudanese proposal to form an international quartet to mediate in the dam dispute. Sudan's prime minister writes to the AU, UN, EU, and US to formally request their mediation in negotiations, but Ethiopia expresses its desire for talks on the dam to continue under the current AU chairmanship. Sudan and Uganda agree to hold a Nile Basin summit. The Ethiopian water minister tells a DR Congo delegation that Ethiopia remains committed to a win-win solution. Ethiopia vows to go ahead with the second phase of the dam filling. It allocates more than $2m to clear forests to pave the way for the second filling. Two senior Ethiopian politicians accuse Egypt and Sudan of working together to destabilise Ethiopia in an attempt to stop the second filling. Several Arab countries express support for Egypt after President Sisi warned that "there would be a state of regional instability" if the country's Nile water rights were violated. A US delegation holds talks with parties involved in the GERD dispute to "learn the facts", expressing support for dialogue to resolve the crisis. The United Arab Emirates proposes a roadmap providing to sign a Declaration on Future Comprehensive Agreement on the Blue Nile, which is not part of the 2015 Declaration of Principles and to start talks from scratch.

## 2021
See also: Explainer: Why are Sudan and Ethiopia locked in escalating border row?
April: Egypt announces the failure of AU-sponsored talks over the GERD held in the DR Congo capital, Kinshasa. The Egyptian irrigation ministry spokesman says Ethiopia has rejected 15 different ideas put forward by Cairo to help resolve the dispute. Sudan's foreign minister voices growing impatience with Ethiopia as it shows "unacceptable intransigence" in the talks. Egypt's foreign minister says any moves by Ethiopia aimed at affecting the country's Nile water share will be regarded as "a hostile act". But Ethiopia's water minister accuses Egypt and Sudan of attempting to undermine the AU-led tripartite negotiations. The Egyptian president warns that "all options are open" if Ethiopia harms his country's water share. Egypt and Sudan turn down an Ethiopian proposal to share data with them before the second filling of the GERD in the rainy season. Sudan's water minister says the Ethiopian offer only focuses on data about testing the GERD gates but ignores the important details on filling and operating the dam and their dates, and the documents that prove the safety of the dam. Egypt and Sudan conduct a joint air force exercise, dubbed Nile Eagles 2, in Sudan. Egypt is engaged in diplomatic manoeuvring and security agreements with several African countries as it rallies African support in the dispute over the Ethiopian dam. Egypt's top diplomat visits six African countries: Kenya, South Africa, Senegal, DR Congo, Tunisia and Comoros. Egyptians online urge the army to carry out a military strike to destroy the dam. Egypt's prime minister warns that Egypt is facing a severe shortage in water resources as it has "entered a phase of abject water poverty, irrespective of the crisis over the GERD".

## 2021
May: The chief Sudanese negotiator on the GERD talks says Ethiopia has technically started the second filling of the dam, and the filling is likely to be completed in July and August. Ethiopia says the GERD will begin a power generation trial run with two turbines and it will carry out cloud seeding to augment the filling of the dam during the rainy season in July and August. Ethiopia condemns Sudan's new claim over territory where Ethiopia's dam is under construction. In unusual remarks, the Egyptian foreign minister says the second filling of Ethiopia's dam will not affect his country's interests, but he warns that Cairo will take action if its water security is jeopardised. Addis Ababa welcomes the Egyptian remarks. The US special envoy to the Horn of Africa, Jeffrey Feltman, visits Egypt, Ethiopia and Sudan as the three countries, especially Egypt, step up diplomatic efforts to drum up support for their position on the GERD. President Sisi says at a meeting with his Congolese counterpart that Egypt will not accept any harm to its water security. In an apparent "message to Ethiopia", Cairo and Khartoum conduct fresh joint military drills dubbed "Guardians of the Nile" between 26 and 31 May. Egyptian army chief of staff Lt Gen Mohamed Farid says the exercise comes amid "surrounding challenges and threats, and the possibility of their escalation". Egypt signs a deal to buy 30 Rafale fighter jets from France, the second such deal in six years, amid increasing popular calls for the country to carry out airstrikes against the dam. Ethiopia's ruling party says the country "will never compromise its national interest" to pressure from external forces. Qatar's foreign minister holds talks in Doha with Ethiopia's state minister for foreign affairs, days after visits to Cairoand Khartoum, with Qatari media hinting at a role for Doha in Ethiopia dam dispute.

## 2021
June: Egypt's foreign minister urges Arab countries to support his country in its dispute with Addis Ababa over the GERD. In the first show of collective Arab support for Egypt and Sudan over the GERD, the Arab League at an extraordinary session in Qatar calls on the UN Security Council to hold an urgent meeting to help launch effective negotiations that ensure a fair and legally binding agreement on the GERD. Ethiopia rejects the "misguided Arab League's positions" in its resolution supporting Egypt and Sudan. It also urges the Arab League to stay out of the Nile dispute and calls on it to leave African issues to Africans and focus on solving problems faced by Arabs. Egypt condemns as asign of "ill intent" remarks by Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed declaring that his country would build 100 dams within a year. Egyptian and Sudanese foreign and irrigation ministers blame Ethiopia for the "failure" of tripartite talks and stress "the need for active intervention by the international community" to resolve the dispute. Egypt's irrigation minister says the current path of AU-sponsored negotiations will not lead to a breakthrough, calls for widening the mediation to include the US, the EU, and the UN. Egypt expresses in a letter to the UN Security Council its rejection of Ethiopia's stated intentions of filling the GERD. Sudan also requests an urgent UNSC session to discuss the Nile dam dispute. Sudan minister travels to Ethiopia for a Nile basin summit. Ethiopia's water minister says his country will proceed with the second filling of the dam.
See also: Explainer: Egypt reaches across Africa amid spat over Ethiopian dam

Ethiopians hold a large rally to back national army and Nile dam filling. Ethiopia's water minister says the amount of water entering the GERD is increasing thanks to heavy rainfall in the country's highlands. Some Egyptian media outlets, however, report Ethiopia's "failure" to complete the second filling of the dam, while President Sisi tries to reassure Egyptians over the potential repercussions of the Ethiopian measure. Egypt's foreign minister says Cairo and Khartoum are able to defend their water interests. Egypt warns at a UNSC session that it will "protect its right to life" if Ethiopia insists on dam filling. The defence minister also says the army is "capable of deterring anyone who would dare to undermine Egypt's security" amid rising tensions with Ethiopia over the announcement on the second filling of the Nile dam. Sudan asks Russia to intervene to help resolve regional tensions over the Nile dam dispute. Egypt and Arab officials urge UN action over the Ethiopian move. Egypt and Sudan hold talks with several African, Arab and European countries to discuss Ethiopian Dam. The UN Security Council urges Sudan, Egypt and Ethiopia to continue AU-led talks on the GERD, at a special emergency session on the Nile Dam dispute on 8 July at Egypt's request. Sudan lashes out at Ethiopia over its letter to the UNSC on Nile dam. Egypt says its decision along with Sudan to go to the UNSC is due to Ethiopia's "intransigence" and attempts to impose a new reality on the ground regarding its Nile dam.
